To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the uniform strong consistency rate of a CDF kernel estimator is the same as that of a density kernel estimator and that (2) a CDF kernel estimate converges uniformly at a faster rate than the density kernel estimate.

(1) the uniform strong consistency of the kernel estimator of CDF holds for all continuous kernels, and the rate of uniform convergence is of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the kernel estimator; and (2) the uniform strong convergence of the kernel estimator is faster than that of the empirical distribution function, and the rate is of order $[n^{-1/4} \log n]$ for the empirical distribution function.
the kernel estimator of a CDF is uniformly strongly consistent with a rate that is faster than the rate of the empirical distribution function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two points.
the uniform consistency of the kernel estimator of a CDF and the rate of convergence of the uniform convergence.
the uniform strong consistency of the kernel estimator of CDFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uniform strong consistency rates are of order $1/\sqrt{n}$.
the rate of uniform strong convergence for the kernel estimator of a CDF is of the same order as that for the kernel estimator for density functions, which is the rate of the order of the bandwidth.
, for any given ε>0, the CDF kernel estimator is strongly consistent with probability 1 and, for a given ε>0 and a kernel K with a bounded support, the rate of uniform convergence is O(n−1/2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate of uniform strong consistency for the kernel estimator of CDF is the same as that of the kernel estimator of probability density function (PDF), and it is faster than that of the empirical distribution function.
the uniform strong consistency rates of kernel CDF estimators are at least as fast as the uniform strong consistency rate of the empirical distribution function.
the uniform strong consistency rates of kernel estimator of the cumulative distribution functions are the same as the empirical distribution functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of convergence of the uniform strong consistency of kernel CDF estimators is not affected by the choice of the kernel.
, under mild conditions, a uniform strong consistency rate of $n^{−1}$ is attainable for the kernel estimator of a CDF, which is the same as that for the empirical distribution function.
the uniform strong consistency rate of the kernel estimator of a CDF depends on both the kernel function and the underlying density function.
